newsitem.title: GREECE: Merrill Lynch is bullish on drachma investments.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch is bullish on drachma investments.

text.p: Greek drachma-denominated debt instruments offer yields of more than 300 basis points above other EU markets and present a good buying opportunity even when compared to many emerging markets, said Merrill Lynch.

"We recommend Greek local currency investments," said Merrill Lynch in its April economic and fixed income investment outlook. "Greek local currency instruments offer yields of more than 300 basis points above those offered by other EU markets."
The report also pointed out that drachma investments offered good value because of their high yields and a small foreign exchange risk component.

With yields of 9.0 to 10 percent and an expected small depreciation of zero to 1.0 percent of the drachma against the ecu this year, $ returns could end up exceeding 500 basis points above ecu funding costs, it said.
The recent weakness of the drachma against the ecu and the likelihood of falling yields called for locking in $ returns of over 8.0 percent, said the report authored by analyst David Calver.

The drachma has slipped by about 1.0 percent versus the ecu year-to-date. The central bank has pre-announced that it wants to keep the drachma broadly stable against the currencies that make up the ecu.
"Further drachma volatility during the course of the year should present similar buying opportunities," it added.
Falling inflation and fiscal consolidation were likely to induce further interest rate cuts rendering 12-month T-bills yields of more than 10 percent particularly attractive.
But the inverted yield curve on government securities highlighted the risk associated with a rollover strategy using 12-month T-bills.
Two-year zeros were a good alternative to the 12-month T-bill strategy because it avoided the short-term rollover risk of T-bills and longer-term risk of a change in exchange rate policy, it added.
FRNs offered higher yields than fixed coupon bonds but were vulnerable to further cuts in the reference 12-month T-bill.
"Fixed-coupon bonds offer 'reasonable value' compared to FRNs," Merrill Lynch said.

Although currency forwards no longer offer higher yields than T-bills, they represent an easy way to access the local market. The 12-month ecu/drachma currency forwards still offer attractive yields around 9.9 percent, it said.
Merrill Lynch said Greek foreign currency debt looks attractive at spreads of 50 to 60 basis points over US treasuries but did not expect anything more than modest gains in the foreseeable future.
"Despite being an EU country, spreads on Greek foreign currency debt are comparable with those of similarly rated emerging markets," it said.

Greece's foreign currency debt enjoys the same credit rating, Baa1, with Czech Republic according to Moody's. S&P gives the same credit rating, BBB-, to Greece, Hungary and Poland but rates Czech Republic with A. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
